questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me, it was important that the university I was going to was going to align with my current education, but it was also very important to choose a place that I could experience a lot in, and be able to try a different culture. I also saw the opportunity to pick a country, where I could easily travel to other cities on weekends, and get to see as much as possbile.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy, our coordinator had before arrival sent a lot of emails with all the important information that we needed upon arrival, and we also met up with him where we could ask questions

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Our coordinator was great at assisting us, and I also asked friends who also were on exchange in Milan

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was pretty easy, we used
spotahome.com
but looked on many sites where they offered short term rentals. The important thing is to make sure that it isn't a scam, and that the neighborhood is safe.
We ended up living in Navigli, which was great

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Just make sure about the distance to the university, and opportunities of public transportation, as well as making sure that you are living in a safe place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
We had received emails regarding our arrival, so when we came to Milan, we went down to our host university and got our proof of arrival, as well as the opportunity to ask questions, and masssimo was a great help. 
Afterwards we needed to change our courses, which could quite easily be done through the host university website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Our coordinator was more than happy to help, and using my own network was also very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I would say I was quite succesful, I did end up changing most of my courses upon arrival, due to them overlapping a lot. Therefore I needed to change half of my courses, but ended up arranging it so I only had one overlap.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Just make sure to check every information you get before arrival, because it will make life a lot easier upon arrival. 
Also be prepared to change your courses once you arrive, to ensure there isn't any overlap, and still then be prepared to have a little overlap, but that is something that you can hardly avoid, but as long as you manage to minimize them and then make sure that your attendances still are registered, then you should be good.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I feel as if the academic level was a bit lower, compared to Denmark, both still good! It felt not quite as technical as it is at University of Copenhagen, which is fair, because I know we are quite far, but it could be felt, also with the classmates that were local.
The exams were also very different.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was quite similar, although I would say it was in general less coordinated then it is here at UCPH. But otherwise I feel it was the same style of teaching most of the time.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Digital Innovation and Management 
Languages of the Media 
Digital Society 
Coding for Computational science

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved Digital Society! The teacher Chris Anderson was great and I learned a lot!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: We had to pay tourist taxes to our apartment upon arrival which was around 180 eur pr person.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
The food and drink at restaurants and bars were cheaper than expected which was very nice! 
The groceries were quite similar to Denmark I would say.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The ESN-programme offered a lot of different events, but this was something I did not took part of, so im not sure what exactly they offered, 
I know they offered trips, picnics, parties and cultural activities, such as museum watching.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Go see the near-by cities and experience more of Italy! 
It is very easy to take a train or a flix-bus to many of the cities for quite cheap which I would highly recommend. For example Como is only one hour away on the trip. 
also during the hot summer days, there are some pool areas within the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
On the weekends, go visit the markets! There are a lot of great ones, my favorites were the Navigli Canal market and the market in Brera. 
Also just go around the different parts of the city and explore, I loved china town and Brera. 
And also to go to other parts of italy on the weekends or days off.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, it has a lot of the same culture, so it wasn't all that different to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
I think maybe the forwardness of some Italians were a bit challenging, or at least something I had to get used to. 
The Italian men were not afraid to look at you or talk, which you had to get used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Just the like classic italian more cultural way to live. Where it is normal to go out to eat, or sit and enjoy a glass of wine after work, the slower paste of life, is something I really appreciated

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Enjoy your time as much as you can, and make sure to visit other parts of Italy, since it is so easy! 
2. Go out to drink and eat, it is so cheap and there are so many good places and opportunities! 
3. Always enjoy the sunny days as much as possible! It rains a lot of the days, so when the sun is out, you have to be outside as well

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
remember to check the weather everyday, in case you need to bring an umbrella. 
Check out all the thrifting/vintage opportunities, both all humanas, but also the vintage stores, there is a great street with 'bivio' and like 7 other thrift stores in one small street.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just getting an experience of a life time, and get the opportunity live in another country for a semester. The experience as a whole is something I will remember for the rest of my life, and that I find very rewarding

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think it might be to have to put your life on pause for half a year, and really try yourself, It is quite a big change that you need to get used to, and you don't have your people from home around you. So I would say the most challenging is missing the people from back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
